title: Rhino Linux 2026.1 Snapshot Release
description: We are happy to announce our 2026.1 snapshot disk image release, along with our launch of UBXI Lomiri images for AMD64/ARM64 Generic ISOs!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Important Pacstall update
description: A recent change in upstream Ubuntu's coreutils (via uutils) causes breakage to Pacstall, and running `rpk update` may prevent Pacstall from being able to update itself. Please manually run `LC_ALL=C pacstall -U` to resolve this issue.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2025.4, and what to expect from us in 2026
description: We are happy to announce our 2025.4 snapshot disk image release! Additionally, we would like to set expectations for what the Rhino Linux Team will be working towards in 2026.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: New Rhino Linux Forums & Emails!
description: Over a year ago we said "We have long-term plans to move discussions away from Discord onto a public-facing forum." We are now happy to announce that our forums are now live! Additionally, we have now finally set up official Rhino Linux email addresses.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2025.3 released, UBports Sponsorship, and a Call for Contributors!
description: It's been a few months since our last disk image release - as usual, we've been hard at work and rolling along, and we are proud of what this snapshot brings together! In addition, we have a new sponsorship and partner, UBports, who will help guide our next upcoming releases, and are making another call for developers and contributors.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: RPK2 out now!
description: At FOSDEM '25, we left the stage with a promise to revive some of our stalled projects. After a long development period, we are proud to be delivering on that promise with the release of RPK2, our rewrite of Rhino PKG in Nushell!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: UBXI KDE 6 Desktop released + RPK2 now in testing!
description: We are proud to announce the release of the first official UBXI port, based on the KDE Plasma 6 desktop environment, as well as calls for testing on our Nushell rewrite of RPK, our meta-package manager. Both projects have been in the works for quite some time, and we are excited to finally bring them to you.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2025.2 - Plenty of patches
description: It's been just about a month since our last snapshot, and we are happy to bring the release of Rhino Linux 2025.2. A lot of development has progressed, with the team working to resolve multiple longer standing issues in our Bug Tracker. Our release notes are shorter this time around, but pack a solid amount of fixes that we hope improve the overall usage and stability of Rhino Linux.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: FOSDEM 2025 - Rhino Linux and Pacstall: Towards a Rolling Ubuntu
description: Rhino Linux will be at FOSDEM 2025! We will be giving a talk on the distros track about the creation, maintenance, and future of Rhino Linux and Pacstall. The talk will be live-streamed and recorded, and we plan to update this blog post with our full script shortly after. Check out the details here, and we hope to see some of you there!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: New Issue Tracker & Hotfix Utility!
description: To improve management of issues, we have consolidated all issue tracking into a new triage repository, and have a new hotfix utility!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2025.1 (& FOSDEM) - Dynamic workspaces, new applications + more!
description: It's been a little while since our last snapshot release. The Rhino has kept on rolling and we are happy to announce the latest disk image release of Rhino Linux. This release comes with a large list of spectacular updates and improvements to the distribution, setting the stage for an amazing year.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Call for Developers and Contributors!
description: Rhino Linux continues to roll along, but as a small team of student developers, our limited resources and manpower can make it challenging to address every issue and suggestion as quickly as we’d like to - and trust us, we want to address them all. We're calling on you to join us in keeping this Rhino rolling, and make it even better. Will you join us?
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2024.2 - New Wiki, Theme, Containers, and so much more!
description: It's been a while since our last disk image release, and this one is packed full of some spectacular changes! Beyond just the distribution, we have also majorly revamped the Rhino Linux wiki. We are pleased to finally present 2024.2 to you!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: An update on Rhino Linux's development goals and structure
description: After a lot of discussions with the Rhino Linux team, we are finally ready to announce changes to the way we develop. We have decided to focus on the following areas...
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Rhino Linux 2024.1 + more
description: After a substantially longer than anticipated development period, we're excited be back and provide our first release of the year.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Important information regarding xz backdoor
description: We know many of you are tired of hearing about the xz backdoor, but we must share important information regarding it. After doing some digging, we confirmed that from Feb 16 to Mar 28 (both of this year), the affected packages were in Ubuntu's noble/devel repositories, directly impacting Rhino Linux.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: ERROR - Evaluating, Rethinking, and Rebalancing Our Rhinos
description: In the Linux community, there is nothing short of 'quite a few tale, of how Linus does not scale' - as our team has found out recently, our team struggles with this exact issue too.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: 2023.4 - Enhancing the Experience, and looking towards 2024
description: After a long development period we're ready to finish off the year with a stellar release, as well as inform you, the community, of what to expect in 2024.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: The Unicorn Beyond XFCE Initiative
description: We announced the development of Rhino Linux one year ago today, and to celebrate our birthday we would like to officially present the “Unicorn Beyond XFCE Initiative” (UBXI).
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: 2023.3 - Quality of life updates!
description: We are proud to announce the disk image release of Rhino Linux 2023.3. This disk image packs the latest and greatest changes we have made to Rhino Linux over this past month of development. Users already running Rhino Linux will already have these changes providing that their systems are kept up to date.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: 2023.2 - Unicorn updates, bug fixes & more!
description: Rhino Linux 2023.2 is the second disk image release we have published. After ~3 weeks of development I am happy to say that it is ready to be shipped. Users already running Rhino Linux should already have the changes if they have upgraded their systems.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: 2023.1 Release - The making of the distro
description: Rhino Linux has now officially moved out of Beta! We have released Rhino Linux 2023.1 on x86_64, ARM, Pine64 and Raspberry Pi devices. For this post we're going to do something a little different and talk about how we developed the distribution.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Beta6 - Your System, PineTab2, RhinoDrop, and more!
description: This beta release brings a flurry of desktop improvements, bug fixes, and under-the-hood improvements to the distribution, as well as a new platform to run Rhino Linux on!
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Beta5 - Unicorn Desktop & issues upgrading.
description: Rhino Linux has had a fair amount of beta releases, mostly fixing smaller issues that have arisen since the first one. We are now happy to announce the release of Rhino Linux 2023.1-beta5. This beta release brings a lot of major changes to Rhino Linux, including the release of our Unicorn Desktop experience.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Open Beta, PinePhone (Pro) & more!
description: Rhino Linux is pleased to announce that it has entered open beta. This is the collective work of multiple contributors and developers. Rhino Linux is designed to work on a variety of devices, including the PinePhone Pro, PinePhone and PineTab.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: The state of Rhino Linux - Development Update
description: Rhino Linux has now been in active development since October 2022. The core vision for the distribution has remained the same throughout the development cycle. Many things have changed since our original announcement detailing the development of the distribution, though.
author: Rhino Linux Team

title: Moving forward with Rolling Rhino Remix
description: Over time, the current development model of Rolling Rhino Remix has become untenable. It started as a passion project with code that is not mature. The project grew quickly, and unfortunately the immature code that makes the distribution is still present today. Rhino Linux will be an Ubuntu-based, rolling release operating system with Ubuntu, Pacstall, and XFCE at the core of the distribution.
author: AJStrong
